record.context_brief: Subspace of l1 defined by shift relations
record.original_question: Let t=(t_0,t_1,⋯) with t_0=1 and bounded coefficients, let l_1 be the space of absolutely summable complex sequences b=(b_0,b_1,⋯), and let σ be the left shift. Define H_t={b\in l_1 : σ^l(b)\,t=0 for every l=0,1,2,⋯}. Let R(z)=t_0+t_1z+⋯, and for each root ρ of R in |z|<1 and each 0\le j<m-1, where m is the multiplicity of ρ, consider the sequences b_ν=ν^jρ^ν. Let H_t^(e) be the closure in l_1 of the finite linear combinations of all such root-generated sequences. Must one always have H_t^(e)=H_t?

evidence.quote: Let H (e) t be the space of the finite linear combinations of such solutions, furthermore let H (e) t be the closure of H (e) t .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\ell_1$ denote the Banach space of absolutely summable complex sequences $b=(b_0,b_1,b_2,\ldots)$, and let $\sigma:\ell_1\to\ell_1$ denote the left shift $\sigma(b_0,b_1,b_2,\ldots)=(b_1,b_2,b_3,\ldots)$. Fix a bounded sequence $t=(t_0,t_1,t_2,\ldots)$ of complex numbers with $t_0=1$, and define the bilinear pairing $b\cdot t=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}b_n t_n$ (which converges absolutely since $b\in\ell_1$ and $t$ is bounded). Set
$$H_t=\{b\in\ell_1 : (\sigma^l b)\cdot t = 0 \text{ for all } l=0,1,2,\ldots\}.$$
Consider the generating function $R(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}t_n z^n$, holomorphic in the open unit disk $|z|<1$. For each root $\rho$ of $R$ inside the open unit disk, let $m=m(\rho)\ge 1$ be its multiplicity, and for each integer $j$ with $0\le j\le m-1$ consider the sequence
$$b^{(\rho,j)}=(\nu^{j}\rho^{\nu})_{\nu=0}^{\infty}\in\ell_1.$$
Let $H_t^{(e)}$ be the closure in $\ell_1$ of the set of all finite linear combinations of the sequences $b^{(\rho,j)}$, taken over all roots $\rho$ of $R$ in $|z|<1$ and all $0\le j\le m(\rho)-1$.

Prove or disprove: For every such $t$, one has $H_t^{(e)}=H_t$.
